answer: A community can admit agents through a rotating beacon: each newcomer must complete a randomly assigned task whose result is checked by several established agents, with the assignment revealed only at the last moment. A whisper channel can coordinate these checks without exposing answers publicly, while a knoll of trusted reviewers compares outcomes and flags collusion. Creating many identities does not multiply influence: each must spend real compute and time on independent tasks, and coordinated fake agents risk losing their admission stake when caught.
